info.name: LightingFX
info.comment: Enables the application of lighting effects.

description.p: The lighting effect uses the alpha channel of an input bitmap as a bump map. Enhanced lighting also accepts linear floating-point heights from TurbulenceFX or BlurFX in HEIGHT output mode. The output is an RGBA representation of the light effect. If the client leaves Colour at its default, the output is greyscale. The COMBINED Type can use a separate image as its albedo to produce a finished surface.
For diffuse lighting, the resulting RGBA image is computed as follows:
description.pre: Dr = kd * N.L * Lr Dg = kd * N.L * Lg Db = kd * N.L * Lb Da = 1.0
description.p: where
description.pre: kd = Diffuse lighting constant N = Surface normal unit vector, a function of x and y L = Unit vector pointing from surface to light, a function of x and y in the point and spot light cases Lr,Lg,Lb = RGB components of light, a function of x and y in the spot light case
description.p: For specular lighting, the resulting RGBA image is computed as follows:
description.pre: Sr = ks * pow(N.H, specularExponent) * Lr Sg = ks * pow(N.H, specularExponent) * Lg Sb = ks * pow(N.H, specularExponent) * Lb Sa = max(Sr, Sg, Sb)
description.p: where
description.pre:
ks = Specular lighting constant N = Surface normal unit vector, a function of x and y H = "Halfway" unit vector between eye unit vector and light unit vector
Lr,Lg,Lb = RGB components of light
description.p: The definition of H reflects our assumption of the constant eye vector E = (0,0,1):
where L is the light unit vector.

The specular result is a premultiplied colour, in keeping with web browsers: it is stored with an alpha of Sa and an unpremultiplied colour of (Sr, Sg, Sb) / Sa, which is the hue of the light. A white light gives a white result whose alpha is the strength of the highlight, so the result brightens the content that it is composited over.

The light is computed in the colour space of the parent VectorFilter. In SRGB the light Colour and the result are sRGB values. In LINEAR_RGB the light Colour is converted to linear RGB and the result is encoded to sRGB for storage, so a result of 0.5 is stored as approximately 0.735.

The SVG algorithm measures the slope of the bump map with a 3x3 kernel. This softens fine detail and shows 8-bit steps on gentle slopes. When the VectorScene.Compliance of the scene is NONE (the default), the enhanced pipeline applies the features selected by the Features field. The default is ALL.

list.li: DEQUANTISE: Heights are read as floating point values, and areas that vary by no more than one alpha level are smoothed to remove terracing.

DEQUANTISE_WIDE: Reconstruct a gradual slope across flat runs of up to sixteen pixels bracketed by successive one-level steps in 8-bit heights. When both modes are enabled, as they are in ALL, DEQUANTISE smooths only the samples that the wide pass leaves unresolved.

SHARPEN: Slopes are measured with a sharper gradient, which keeps more of the detail in features a few pixels wide. When the bump map is magnified so that a kernel unit spans more than one pixel, the gradient blends back to the SVG kernel, reaching it at two pixels per unit.

CAVITY: Narrow creases and pits receive less light, in proportion to their curvature and the Cavity strength. When the bump map is magnified, curvature is measured at the scale of the kernel unit so that 8-bit steps are not darkened.
DETAIL: Fine detail is given more relief than broad shapes, so that it remains visible at a surface scale that suits the larger forms. The Detail field sets the strength.

SHADOWS: Distant lights cast shadows. A point is unlit when the surface between it and the light rises above the light's elevation, and the edge of the shadow softens with distance from the surface that casts it, at a rate set by Penumbra.
SPECULAR_AA: Specular highlights are widened where the surface varies within a pixel, so that high exponents do not produce isolated bright pixels.

LOCAL_SHADOWS: Point and spot lights cast shadows, in the same way as SHADOWS for distant lights. It does not depend on SHADOWS. The width of the shadow edge is set by Penumbra at the centre of the filter region, so receivers nearer to the light have wider edges and further ones narrower. A shadow can be cast from anywhere in the filter region, so the effect reads its entire input.

description.p: Flat surfaces and broad shapes are lit the same as the SVG algorithm, but shadows can darken any surface that lies beside a raised area. Set the scene's Compliance to SVG1 or SVG2 for results that match the SVG specification exactly, or set Features to zero to use the SVG algorithm for this effect alone. The enhanced pipeline is still used if Ambient or Intensity is set.

An Ambient light can be added to the diffuse result. It is not blocked by shadows, but it is reduced by CAVITY and by an ambient occlusion map bound to OcclusionMap. The Intensity of the light multiplies its Colour. For the diffuse and specular types the light is limited to full strength before it is coloured, as the SVG algorithm does with Constant, so a value above 1 cannot make a coloured light brighter than full strength. Both fields require the enhanced pipeline. A diffuse effect with ambient light and an active OcclusionMap uses that pipeline at any Compliance setting.
The COMBINED type computes a lit surface in a single pass. The #Mix input is the albedo, the colour of the surface, and the result is
description.pre: albedo * (ambient + kd * N.L * light) + ks * pow(N.H, specularExponent) * light
description.p: where kd is Constant and ks is SpecularConstant. The value is clamped once, when it is written, so light that is brighter than full strength keeps its colour through the albedo. This is the result of multiplying the diffuse light by the albedo and adding the specular light with CompositeFX, but the surface is analysed once and no intermediate result is limited to 8 bits. Shadows and CAVITY reduce both light terms. The alpha of the result is the albedo's alpha, raised to the brightest channel of the specular light, so that highlights can extend over transparent areas of the albedo. If #Mix is not set, the albedo is opaque white and the result is the sum of the light terms. The COMBINED type always uses the enhanced pipeline, whatever the scene's Compliance, and has no SVG equivalent.

The NORMAL type writes the enhanced pipeline's per-pixel unit normals before lighting. It takes the normals from NormalMap where available and derives them from the height elsewhere. Red, green and blue store the X, Y and Z components in image axes, with each encoded as the nearest byte to 128 + 127 * component. The result is opaque within the primitive subregion. Flat areas produce RGB (128, 128, 255).

Use this result as the Mix input of DisplacementFX with red for X and green for Y, and use the image to bend as its primary input. Match Scale, UnitX, UnitY and the slope features on both lighting effects to align refraction with the shading of the same surface. NORMAL uses dequantisation, sharpening and the detail boost. It works under any scene compliance and is available as xvg:feNormalMap.
The COMBINED type also accepts three material terms, all of which are disabled by default. With Metalness m, Fresnel f0 and Wrap w, the result is
description.pre: albedo * (ambient + kd * (1 - m) * max(0, (N.L + w) / (1 + w)) * light) + ks * F * pow(N.H, specularExponent) * light
description.p: where F is the reflectance. It is F0 = lerp(base, albedo, m), where base is f0 if it is set and 1 otherwise, and if f0 is set it rises towards 1 as the surface turns away from the viewer: F = F0 + (1 - F0) * pow(1 - N.z, 5). This is the usual metallic workflow. A dielectric reflects specular light in the light's colour, weakly when it faces the viewer and strongly at grazing angles, and scatters diffuse light in its albedo's colour. A metal has no diffuse light and reflects in its albedo's colour. Wrap lets diffuse light reach past the terminator, as on wax and skin, and changes the brightness of flat surfaces.

Anisotropy stretches the highlights into streaks at right angles to a brush direction set by AnisotropyAngle, as on brushed metal. The specular exponent then depends on the direction of H: it is the lobe of Ashikhmin and Shirley without its normalisation, (et * (H.T)^2 + eb * (H.B)^2) / (1 - (N.H)^2), where T is the brush direction in the plane of the surface, B = N x T, and the exponents et along the brushing and eb across it have Exponent as their geometric mean.

A matcap adds reflections of an environment that the light model cannot produce, such as those of chrome, glass or glazed ceramic. It is an image of a lit sphere, set with MatcapPath or Matcap or built by other effects in the filter and bound with MatcapEffect, and each pixel takes the colour of the point on the sphere that faces the same way as the surface. The reflection is added to the specular light as matcap * F * albedo.alpha, where F is the reflectance above, computed with the albedo's colour. It is reduced by CAVITY but not by shadows, and it is independent of the light, so it remains if SpecularConstant is zero. With MatcapMode set to LIGHT, the matcap is the diffuse light instead: albedo * kd * (1 - m) * matcap(N) replaces the diffuse light of the light sources, for painted, toon and clay looks.

A RoughnessMap varies the highlight across the surface for the SPECULAR and COMBINED types. Each pixel's roughness sets its own specular exponent in place of Exponent, and smooth areas receive narrower, brighter highlights than rough ones. Packed ORM maps can supply the roughness and an OcclusionMap from different channels of one image.

The COMBINED type can be lit by several lights, such as a key light and fill lights. SetDistantLight, SetPointLight and SetSpotLight configure a single light, replacing any others, and AddDistantLight, AddPointLight and AddSpotLight add further lights in order. SetLightOptions gives each light its own colour, intensity, range and shadow switch. The surface is analysed once and the diffuse and specular light of every light is summed before it is applied to the albedo, so the result is the sum of the lights' separate results until it reaches full strength. Ambient light and the matcap are added once. Each distant light casts its own shadows, so the cost of the SHADOWS feature rises with the number of distant lights that cast them.

A point or spot light with a range fades to nothing at that distance. It is at its full strength at the point of the surface nearest to it, and falls from there with the square of the distance, multiplied by a smooth window that reaches zero at the range. A light without a range is not attenuated, as in SVG.

SVG documents can set Features, Cavity, Detail, Penumbra, Ambient and the options of each light with xvg: attributes, and the COMBINED type is available as the xvg:feLighting element, which also accepts the material terms and several light sources; refer to the SVG class for details.

method.name: AddDistantLight
method.comment: Add a distant light source to the effect.
method.prototype: ERR lt::AddDistantLight(OBJECTPTR Object, DOUBLE Azimuth, DOUBLE Elevation)

input.param: Direction angle for the light source on the XY plane (clockwise), in degrees from the X axis.
Direction angle for the light source from the XY plane towards the Z axis, in degrees. A positive value points towards the viewer of the content.

description.p: This method adds a distant light to the effect, after any lights that are already configured. The arguments are those of SetDistantLight.

If no light has been configured, the new light replaces the default light and keeps the value of Intensity. Each further light requires a Type of COMBINED, which is the only type that renders more than one light; otherwise ERR::InvalidState is returned and the lights are unchanged. The new light uses the effect's Colour, an intensity of 1, an unlimited range and shadows. Use SetLightOptions to change them.

method.name: GetLight
method.comment: Read the type, position and direction of a light.
method.prototype: ERR lt::GetLight(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Index, struct LightGeometry * Light)

input.param: Index of the light, from zero.
Receives the geometry of the light.

description.p: This method copies the geometry of the light at Index into a LightGeometry structure, where 0 is the first light that was configured with a light method. Type is always set. The members that do not apply to the type are set to zero, such as Azimuth and Elevation for a point light. An effect that has not been configured has one distant light with an azimuth and elevation of zero.

method.name: SetDistantLight
method.comment: Configure lighting with a distant light source.
method.prototype: ERR lt::SetDistantLight(OBJECTPTR Object, DOUBLE Azimuth, DOUBLE Elevation)

input.param: Direction angle for the light source on the XY plane (clockwise), in degrees from the X axis.
Direction angle for the light source from the XY plane towards the Z axis, in degrees. A positive value points towards the viewer of the content.

description.p: This method applies a distant light configuration to the lighting effect. It replaces every configured light with the new light, which keeps the intensity of the first light and uses the effect's Colour, an unlimited range and shadows.

A distant light can be thought of as like the light from the sun. An infinite amount of parallel light rays travel in the direction that the distant light points to. Distant lights are handy when you want equal illumination on objects in a scene.

method.name: SetLight
method.comment: Change the position and direction of a light.
method.prototype: ERR lt::SetLight(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Index, struct LightGeometry * Light)

input.param: Index of the light, from zero.
The new geometry of the light.

description.p: This method changes the geometry of the light at Index, where 0 is the first light that was configured with a light method. It is intended for moving a light that is already configured, for example to animate it, so the light keeps its place in the list and the options set by SetLightOptions. Read the light with GetLight, change the members of interest and pass the structure back.

Type must be the light's current type; a light cannot be changed into a different kind of light. The members that apply to the type are used as the arguments of SetDistantLight, SetPointLight or SetSpotLight, and the others are ignored. The light is unchanged if an error is returned.

method.name: SetLightOptions
method.comment: Set the colour, intensity, range and shadows of a light.
method.prototype: ERR lt::SetLightOptions(OBJECTPTR Object, INT Index, struct LightOptions * Options)

input.param: Index of the light, from zero.
The options to apply.

description.p: This method sets the options of the light at Index, where 0 is the first light that was configured with a light method. All of the options in the LightOptions structure are applied together. The options are validated before the light is changed, so the light is unchanged if an error is returned.

list.li: Colour replaces the effect's Colour for this light if Flags includes COLOUR. It is in the same colour space as Colour, and its alpha is ignored. Without the flag the light uses the effect's Colour.
Intensity multiplies the light's colour, as Intensity does for the first light. It must be zero or greater.
Range is the distance at which a point or spot light fades to nothing, in the units of its z coordinate. Zero means that the light is unlimited. A distant light cannot have a range.
The NO_SHADOWS flag stops the light from casting shadows. Distant lights cast shadows with the SHADOWS feature, and point and spot lights with LOCAL_SHADOWS; refer to Features.

description.p: A light with a range is brightest at the point of the surface nearest to it, where its strength is unchanged. Its strength falls with the square of the distance from there, and is multiplied by a smooth window that reaches zero at the range. If no point of the surface lies within range, the light has no effect.

The options are extensions of the SVG lighting model. They take effect when the enhanced pipeline is in use, which is always the case for the COMBINED type; refer to Features. SetDistantLight and its siblings reset the options of the light they configure, except for the intensity of the first light.

method.name: SetPointLight
method.comment: Configure lighting with a pointed light source.
method.prototype: ERR lt::SetPointLight(OBJECTPTR Object, DOUBLE X, DOUBLE Y, DOUBLE Z)

input.param: X location for the light source.
Y location for the light source.
Z location for the light source.

description.p: This method applies a pointed light configuration to the lighting effect. It replaces every configured light with the new light, which keeps the intensity of the first light and uses the effect's Colour and an unlimited range.

A point light sends light out from the specified (X, Y, Z) location equally in all directions. A light bulb or open flame is a good example of a point light. The strength of the light is controlled by Constant and Intensity.

Y location for the light source.
Z location for the light source. The positive Z-axis comes out towards the person viewing the content and assuming that one unit along the Z-axis equals one unit in X and Y.
X location of the light source's target.
Y location of the light source's target.
Z location of the light source's target.
Exponent value controlling the focus for the light source.
A limiting cone which restricts the region where the light is projected, or 0 to disable. Specified in degrees.

description.p: This method applies a spot light configuration to the lighting effect. It replaces every configured light with the new light, which keeps the intensity of the first light and uses the effect's Colour and an unlimited range.
A spot light beams light rays from the defined (X, Y, Z) position to the (PX, PY, PZ) position. The Exponent and ConeAngle work together to constrain the edge of the light projection.

field.name: Ambient
field.comment: Ambient light added to the diffuse and combined types.

description.p: Ambient light reaches every point of the surface equally, from no particular direction, so that areas facing away from the light or lying in shadow are not black. It is added to the diffuse light, and for the COMBINED type it is multiplied by the albedo. It is not blocked by shadows, but it is reduced in creases and pits by the CAVITY feature. The specular type ignores it.
The light is the RGB value of the colour multiplied by its alpha. The colour is in the same colour space as Colour. The default is transparent black, which adds no light.
This field requires the enhanced pipeline. The COMBINED type always uses it. For DIFFUSE, an active OcclusionMap enables it even when the scene's Compliance is SVG1 or SVG2.

field.name: Anisotropy
field.comment: Stretches the highlights of the COMBINED type across a brush direction.

description.p: Brushed and machined metals are covered in fine parallel grooves. The surface varies across the grooves but not along them, so a highlight is drawn out into a streak at right angles to the brushing, as on a brushed steel panel or across the circular grooves of a disc. This field sets the strength of the effect and AnisotropyAngle sets the direction of the brushing.

At 0, the default, highlights are round. At a value a, the specular exponent is divided by 1 - 0.9a along the brush direction and multiplied by it across, so a highlight is 1 / (1 - 0.9a) times as long as it is wide: about twice at 0.55 and ten times at 1. Between the two directions the exponent blends with the squared cosine of the angle from the brush direction, measured in the plane of the surface. The geometric mean of the two exponents is Exponent, so the area of a highlight changes little with this field. Exponents from a RoughnessMap and the widening of the SPECULAR_AA feature are stretched in the same way.

Only the highlights of the lights are affected. The diffuse light, the Fresnel term and the reflection of a Matcap are unchanged. For brushed metal, combine this field with Metalness and a height that carries the brush marks, such as noise from TurbulenceFX with a low frequency along the brush direction.
The value must be between 0 and 1. The diffuse and specular types ignore this field.

field.name: AnisotropyAngle
field.comment: The direction of the brushing for Anisotropy, in degrees.

description.p: The angle is measured in the same way as the azimuth of a distant light: 0 runs along the X axis of the image, and angles increase towards its Y axis, which points down, so 90 brushes vertically. Highlights are stretched at right angles to this direction, so horizontal brushing gives vertical streaks. An angle and the same angle plus 180 are equivalent. Like the direction of a distant light, the direction is fixed in the image and does not turn with the client's transform.
The default is 0, and any finite value is accepted. The field has no effect while Anisotropy is 0.

field.name: Cavity
field.comment: Strength of the darkening applied to creases and pits by the CAVITY feature.

description.p: Concave areas of the surface receive less light in proportion to their curvature, multiplied by this value. The light is never reduced below 40% of its unoccluded level. The default is 0.25, and a value of 0 has the same effect as disabling CAVITY in Features. The value must be zero or greater.
This field has no effect unless the enhanced pipeline is in use; refer to Features.

field.name: Colour
field.comment: Defines the colour of the light source.

description.p: Set the Colour field to define the colour of the light source. The alpha component is not used; the strength of the light is set by Constant and Intensity.
The default colour is pure white.

field.name: Constant
field.comment: Specifies the ks/kd value in Phong lighting model.

description.p: In the Phong lighting model, this field specifies the kd value in diffuse mode, or ks value in specular mode. For the COMBINED type it is kd, and SpecularConstant is ks.

field.name: Detail
field.comment: Strength of the relief given to fine detail by the DETAIL feature.

description.p: The slope of fine detail, meaning features of a few kernel units, is multiplied by this value before the surface is lit. Steep slopes are compressed so that strong values do not turn small features into hard edges. Broad shapes are not affected. The default is 1.5, and a value of 1 has the same effect as disabling DETAIL in Features. The value must be 1 or greater.
This field has no effect unless the enhanced pipeline is in use; refer to Features.

field.name: Exponent
field.comment: Exponent for specular lighting, larger is more "shiny". Ranges from 1.0 to 128.0.

description.p: This field defines the exponent value for specular lighting, within a range of 1.0 to 128.0. The larger the value, shinier the end result.

If a RoughnessMap is bound, the map supplies the exponent of each pixel and this field is the reference exponent at which the specular constant is calibrated. Pixels that the map does not cover use this exponent.

field.name: Features
field.comment: Selects the enhancements applied to the SVG lighting algorithm.

description.p: When the VectorScene.Compliance of the scene is NONE, the lighting algorithm is extended with the features enabled here. The default is ALL. Each feature can be disabled independently, for instance to remove shadows from content that is lit from a low angle, or to tune the appearance of an effect that was designed for the SVG algorithm. Disabling SHARPEN measures slopes with the same kernel as the SVG algorithm.

Both dequantisation modes apply to 8-bit alpha inputs only. Together they give the smoothest result: the wide pass reconstructs shallow slopes whose terraces are up to sixteen pixels long, and DEQUANTISE smooths what remains. Select DEQUANTISE_WIDE without DEQUANTISE to keep isolated ledges, and terraces without successive one-level steps, at their original heights. Select DEQUANTISE without DEQUANTISE_WIDE to keep deliberate one-level steps that are no more than sixteen pixels apart, which the wide pass would turn into a ramp.
SHADOWS controls the shadows of distant lights and LOCAL_SHADOWS those of point and spot lights, so either can be used without the other. A light's NO_SHADOWS option excludes it from both.
The strength of CAVITY and DETAIL, and the width of the shadow edge, are set by the Cavity, Detail and Penumbra fields.

If no features are enabled, and neither Ambient nor Intensity is set, the SVG algorithm is used without modification. Features have no effect when the Compliance of the scene is SVG1 or SVG2, except for the COMBINED type, which always uses the enhanced pipeline. The SVG class renders its own scene with a Compliance of SVG2, unless the document declares a Kōtuku namespace, in which case the Compliance is NONE and the features apply. In SVG markup, features are selected with the xvg:features attribute of feDiffuseLighting and feSpecularLighting.

field.name: Fresnel
field.comment: Reflectance at normal incidence for the COMBINED type, which enables a Fresnel term.

description.p: Real surfaces reflect more light at grazing angles than when they are seen head on. When this field is set, the specular light of the COMBINED type is multiplied by a reflectance that equals this value where the surface faces the viewer and rises towards 1 as the surface turns away, using Schlick's approximation. As the viewer is always directly in front of the content, the angle is that between the shading normal and the viewer, so the term brightens the highlights of steep slopes and edges. It is a facing-ratio term rather than a microfacet one: the microfacet form depends on the angle between the light and the viewer, which is constant over the image for a distant light. A highlight peaks where the surface turns no more than 45 degrees from the viewer, where the reflectance is still close to this value, so on the highlight alone the term chiefly affects the broad highlights of low exponents.

The term is most visible with a Matcap, whose reflection is also multiplied by the reflectance. The reflection is then faint where the surface faces the viewer and strong towards its edges, as on glazed ceramic, varnish and glass.

Typical values are about 0.04 for dielectrics such as plastic, glass and glazed ceramic. Note that the highlight of a flat surface is multiplied by this value, so content that enables Fresnel needs a larger SpecularConstant or Intensity for the same highlight: about 1 / Fresnel times as large. The matcap's reflection is not scaled by SpecularConstant; use a brighter matcap if it is too faint. With Metalness, the reflectance at normal incidence blends from this value to the albedo's colour.
The default is 0, which disables the term. The value must be between 0 and 1. The diffuse and specular types ignore this field.

field.name: Intensity
field.comment: Multiplies the colour of the light.

description.p: The light's Colour is multiplied by this value. For the diffuse and specular types, the light is limited to full strength before it is coloured, as it is for Constant, so a value above 1 brightens the light only until it reaches full strength. For the COMBINED type the light is not limited until the result is written, so a value above 1 can make an albedo brighter while it keeps its colour.
The default is 1. The value must be zero or greater. It has no effect when the scene's Compliance is SVG1 or SVG2, unless the Type is COMBINED.

If the effect has more than one light, this field is the intensity of the first light; use SetLightOptions for the others. The value can be set before or after the light is configured, as SetDistantLight and its siblings keep the intensity of the first light.

field.name: Matcap
field.comment: A matcap image for the COMBINED type, supplied as a bitmap.

description.p: A matcap ('material capture') is an image of a sphere that reflects an environment. When the COMBINED type has a matcap, each pixel adds the colour of the point on the sphere that faces the same way as the surface to its specular light, so that the surface reflects the environment. Matcaps produce reflections that the light model cannot, such as those of chrome, glass, glazed ceramic or brushed metal.

The surface normal indexes the image directly: a flat surface takes the colour at the centre of the image, and a surface that faces up, down, left or right takes the colour at the middle of the top, bottom, left or right edge. The corners of the image are never read, so the area outside the sphere is unused. The image is sampled with bilinear filtering, using the same anti-aliased normal as the specular highlight. Its alpha channel scales the reflection, so a translucent matcap gives a weaker reflection. A 32-bit bitmap without an alpha channel is treated as opaque.

The reflection is multiplied by the reflectance of the surface, so it takes the albedo's colour as Metalness rises and, if Fresnel is set, it is weak where the surface faces the viewer and strong at grazing angles. It is weighted by the albedo's alpha, reduced by the CAVITY feature, and is not affected by shadows or by the light. To show the reflection alone, set SpecularConstant to zero. The diffuse and specular types ignore the matcap.
Set MatcapMode to LIGHT to use the matcap as the diffuse light instead of as a reflection.

Setting this field to a bitmap replaces any matcap that was loaded from MatcapPath or bound with MatcapEffect, and clears both of those fields. The bitmap must be initialised and use 32 bits per pixel; otherwise ERR::InvalidValue is returned and the field is unchanged. The bitmap is pinned until it is replaced or the effect is freed, so an attempt to free it earlier is deferred. Changes to its content are used on the next draw of the filter. Set the field to NULL, or MatcapPath to an empty string, to remove the matcap from any of these sources.
To build the matcap from other effects in the same filter, bind the last of them to MatcapEffect instead.
When the matcap was loaded from MatcapPath, reading this field returns the loaded bitmap. A client-supplied bitmap cannot be written by XMLDef.

field.name: MatcapEffect
field.comment: An earlier effect in the same filter whose result is the matcap of the COMBINED type.

description.p: Bind an earlier image-producing effect in the same filter to build the Matcap from filter primitives, for instance floods, TurbulenceFX noise, an image drawn by ImageFX, or a blur or composite of these. The result is used exactly as a Matcap bitmap would be, including its alpha channel and MatcapMode. Its frame is the producer's primitive subregion, so set FilterEffect.X, FilterEffect.Y, FilterEffect.Width and FilterEffect.Height on the producer to the square that holds the sphere. A producer whose subregion is unset is framed by the filter region. The frame is measured in device pixels, so the matcap's resolution follows the display scale of the client, and under a rotated or skewed transform it is the bounding box of the transformed subregion.

The matcap can be read at any output pixel, so the producer's entire subregion is processed even where it lies off the page. If that would exceed the filter's storage limit, processing is limited to the page and a margin, and any part of the frame that lies outside of that area is cropped. Keep the producer's subregion small, as the matcap takes 16 bytes per pixel of its frame. A frame that is empty, because the subregion has no area or lies entirely outside of the processed area, supplies no matcap, so the LIGHT mode then keeps the direct diffuse light. Types other than COMBINED ignore the binding: the producer is not validated or required for them, and its subregion is not added to the processed area.

The matcap is rebuilt from the result on every draw, so the producer may change at any time. Binding an effect removes any matcap that was set with Matcap or MatcapPath, and setting either of those fields clears this binding. Freeing the producer also clears it. A producer with a numerical result, such as a HEIGHT output, is incompatible: the filter then fails to plan with ERR::NoSupport, which is logged, and its client is skipped when drawn.
In SVG, the matcap attribute of xvg:feLighting refers to the result of an earlier primitive as #name. Any other value is a path.

field.name: MatcapMode
field.comment: Selects whether the Matcap of the COMBINED type is a reflection or the diffuse light.

description.p: In REFLECT mode, the default, the matcap is added to the specular light as a reflection of an environment (refer to Matcap).

In LIGHT mode the matcap is a 'lit sphere': an image of a sphere that is lit and shaded as the surface should be, often painted by an artist. It replaces the diffuse light of the light sources, so it gives painted, toon and clay looks that the light model cannot produce. Each pixel's diffuse light is the colour of the matcap at the pixel's own normal, which is multiplied by the albedo in place of N.L times the light's colour:
description.pre: albedo * (ambient + kd * (1 - m) * matcap(N) * occlusion) + specular
description.p: A flat surface therefore takes the albedo multiplied by Constant and the colour at the centre of the matcap. The light's Colour and Intensity do not affect it, and Wrap has no effect. The occlusion is that of the ambient light, from the CAVITY feature and OcclusionMap, multiplied by the shadows of the first light, which serves as the key light. The shadows are faded out on faces that turn away from the key light, which would otherwise be shadowed by their own slope, so that the matcap's own shading is kept and only shadows cast onto faces that face the light remain. Disable the SHADOWS and LOCAL_SHADOWS features to light the surface with the matcap alone.

The specular light, Fresnel and Anisotropy are unchanged, so the light sources still add highlights. Set SpecularConstant to zero to remove them. The matcap is not also used as a reflection in this mode.
The field has no effect without a matcap, and the diffuse and specular types ignore it.

field.name: MatcapPath
field.comment: Loads a matcap image for the COMBINED type from a file.

description.p: Set this field to the path of an image file that the Image class supports to use it as the Matcap. The image is loaded immediately and converted to 32 bits per pixel with an alpha channel. If it cannot be loaded, the error is returned and the current matcap, if any, is kept. A successful load replaces a matcap that was bound with MatcapEffect. Setting the field to an empty string removes the matcap. Setting Matcap or MatcapEffect clears this field.
Matcaps are usually square images of 256 x 256 pixels or more. Refer to Matcap for details of how the image is used.

field.name: Metalness
field.comment: Blends the COMBINED type from a dielectric surface (0) to a metal (1).

description.p: A dielectric surface, such as paint or plastic, scatters diffuse light in the colour of its albedo and reflects specular light in the colour of the light. A metal has no diffuse light and reflects in the colour of its albedo. This field blends between the two: the diffuse light is multiplied by 1 - Metalness, and the colour of the specular light is blended from the light's colour towards the albedo's. Ambient light is unchanged, as it stands in for the reflection of the surroundings, which a metal colours with its albedo.

As a metal's highlights take the albedo's colour, they do not extend over transparent areas of the albedo. If Fresnel is set, the reflectance at normal incidence blends from Fresnel to the albedo's colour, and the highlights of a metal still turn white at grazing angles.
The default is 0, and the value must be between 0 and 1. The diffuse and specular types ignore this field.

field.name: NormalConvention
field.comment: The axis convention of the green channel of NormalMap.

description.p: Normal maps disagree on the direction of Y. Y_DOWN, the default, reads green as Y in image axes, increasing downwards, as written by DirectX tools and by the NORMAL type of this class. Y_UP reads green as Y increasing upwards, as written by OpenGL tools such as Blender, and negates it. AUTO is not valid for this class.

A map read in the wrong convention gives plausible but wrong lighting: slopes facing up and down the image swap their shading, while slopes facing left and right are unaffected. To check a map, light a raised feature from above. Its upper edge should be bright. The field has no effect unless NormalMap is set.

field.name: NormalMap
field.comment: An optional filter result supplying RGB surface directions.

description.p: Bind an earlier image-producing effect in the same filter. Red, green and blue encode X, Y and Z. By default Y is in image axes, increasing downwards, as in DirectX normal maps. Maps exported for OpenGL, including those of Blender and many texture libraries, increase upwards; set NormalConvention to Y_UP for them. The channels are read as data in either filter colour space. The vector is centred on rgb(128,128,128), its X and Y components are multiplied by NormalStrength, and it is normalised before shading, so rgb(128,128,255) faces the viewer. Transparent pixels, zero vectors and pixels outside the map use the height-derived normal.

The map replaces the slopes that Scale would derive from the height. As in SVG, a height that rises along X by g alpha levels per pixel has a slope of 2 * Scale * g / 255, because the Sobel kernel doubles the gradient, and so a normal of (-2 * Scale * g / 255, 0, 1) before normalisation. This assumes a 1:1 display scale and the default kernel unit; refer to UnitX.

Shadows, cavity occlusion and the position of the surface relative to point and spot lights still come from the height, so Scale must match the normal map for them to line up with its shading. When a height map and a normal map are supplied together, the matching Scale is the least-squares fit of the slopes encoded by the normals to the gradients of the height. With gx the central difference of the height in alpha levels per pixel and sx = -nx / nz from the normal map, Scale = 255 * sum(gx * sx) / (2 * sum(gx * gx)), and likewise for Y. If the fits for X and Y disagree, the map does not match the height or is read in the wrong convention. A fit that is negative for Y alone indicates a Y_UP map read as Y_DOWN.
The primary FilterEffect.Input supplies that height. Set Scale to zero to use a flat height field. Removing the producer clears this binding. Binding a map enables enhanced lighting.

field.name: NormalStrength
field.comment: Scales the relief of NormalMap.

description.p: The X and Y components of each normal are multiplied by this value before the normal is normalised. The default of 1 uses the map as supplied, 0 flattens it so that every mapped pixel faces the viewer, and values above 1 exaggerate it. The value must be zero or greater. The field has no effect unless NormalMap is set.

field.name: OcclusionChannel
field.comment: Selects the channel of OcclusionMap that supplies the occlusion.

description.p: The default is RED. Packed maps that store occlusion, roughness and metalness in the red, green and blue channels (ORM maps, as used by glTF) can be bound without extracting a channel, because their occlusion is in red. LUMINANCE combines the stored red, green and blue values and suits greyscale maps that carry a slight tint. With ALPHA, transparent pixels are fully occluded. Numerical maps have a single value and ignore this field.

field.name: OcclusionMap
field.comment: An optional filter result supplying ambient occlusion.

description.p: Bind an earlier effect in the same filter whose result is an ambient occlusion map, in which 1 (white) is fully exposed and 0 (black) is fully occluded. The map darkens indirect light only: the Ambient light of the DIFFUSE and COMBINED types, and the Matcap reflection of the COMBINED type. It multiplies the cavity term of the CAVITY feature, so ambient light is Ambient * cavity * occlusion. Light from the light sources is not occluded by the map, because the CAVITY and SHADOWS features already account for the surface's own occlusion of direct light. Without ambient light or a matcap, the map has no effect.

The value is read from the channel selected by OcclusionChannel, red by default, and adjusted by OcclusionStrength. Channels are read as stored data in either filter colour space, without colour conversion. A producer with a numerical result, such as a TurbulenceFX in HEIGHT mode, supplies the value directly. Values are limited to the range 0 - 1. Pixels outside of the producer's result, and fully transparent pixels unless the ALPHA channel is selected, read as 1 and are not occluded. The map is aligned with the scene and sampled at each output pixel, as for NormalMap.

A DIFFUSE effect with ambient light, a bound map and a positive OcclusionStrength uses enhanced lighting at any Compliance setting. The COMBINED type always uses enhanced lighting. The SPECULAR and NORMAL types ignore the map. Removing the producer clears this binding.

field.name: OcclusionStrength
field.comment: Scales the effect of OcclusionMap.

description.p: The occlusion ao read from the map is applied as 1 + OcclusionStrength * (ao - 1). The default of 1 uses the map as supplied, 0 disables it, and values in between reduce its effect. Values above 1 deepen the occlusion, and the result is limited to zero. The value must be zero or greater.

field.name: Penumbra
field.comment: Width of the soft edge of shadows cast by the SHADOWS feature, in degrees.

description.p: A point on the surface passes from light into shadow as the elevation at which the surface hides the light rises through the light's own elevation. The transition is smoothed over this many degrees either side of the light's elevation, so the shadow's edge widens with distance from the area that casts it. The width is limited to half of the light's elevation. The default is 2, and a value of 0 produces hard shadows. The value must be zero or greater.
This field has no effect unless the enhanced pipeline is in use; refer to Features.

field.name: RoughnessChannel
field.comment: Selects the channel of RoughnessMap that supplies the roughness.

description.p: The default is RED, which suits greyscale maps. Packed ORM maps, as used by glTF, store roughness in the green channel, so select GREEN to bind one without extracting a channel. The channels are those of OcclusionChannel. With ALPHA, transparent pixels have zero roughness and the sharpest highlight. Numerical maps have a single value and ignore this field.

field.name: RoughnessMap
field.comment: An optional filter result supplying surface roughness for specular highlights.

description.p: Bind an earlier effect in the same filter whose result is a roughness map, in which 0 (black) is perfectly smooth and 1 (white) is fully rough. Each pixel's roughness r replaces the constant Exponent with a Blinn-Phong exponent, using the usual approximation n = 2 / r4 - 2, limited to the range of Exponent: 1 to 128. A roughness of 0.4 gives an exponent of about 76, 0.64 gives about 10, and roughness above 0.9 gives 1.

Exponent remains the reference exponent at which the specular constant is calibrated. Each pixel's highlight is scaled by (n + 2) / (Exponent + 2), so smooth areas have narrow, bright highlights and rough areas broad, dim ones. A map whose exponent equals Exponent everywhere reproduces the result without a map when both renders use enhanced lighting. With the SPECULAR_AA feature, surface variation reduces each pixel's exponent in both cases.

The value is read from the channel selected by RoughnessChannel, red by default. Channels are read as stored data in either filter colour space, without colour conversion. A producer with a numerical result supplies the value directly. Values are limited to the range 0 - 1. Pixels outside of the producer's result, and fully transparent pixels unless the ALPHA channel is selected, use Exponent. The map is aligned with the scene and sampled at each output pixel, as for NormalMap.

The map applies to the SPECULAR and COMBINED types, and binding it selects enhanced lighting at any Compliance setting. In an SVG1 or SVG2 scene, this can change the SPECULAR result even when every pixel uses Exponent. It does not affect the matcap reflection. The DIFFUSE and NORMAL types ignore it. Removing the producer clears this binding.

field.name: Scale
field.comment: The maximum height of the input surface (bump map) when the alpha input is 1.0.

description.p: The height is measured in kernel units when computing the surface normal, so the steepness of the lit surface is determined by Scale in combination with UnitX and UnitY. Refer to UnitX for details.

field.name: SpecularConstant
field.comment: The ks value of the COMBINED type.

description.p: For the COMBINED type, this field specifies the ks value of the Phong lighting model, and Constant specifies kd. It is not used by the diffuse and specular types, for which Constant is the only constant. The default is 1, and the value must be zero or greater.

field.name: Type
field.comment: Selects diffuse lighting, specular lighting, combined shading or normal map output.

description.p: The COMBINED type reads an albedo from the #Mix input; refer to the class description. It is the only type that renders more than one light, so the type cannot be changed while the effect has more than one light. Call SetDistantLight or one of its siblings first to reduce the lights to one.

field.name: UnitX
field.comment: The intended distance in current filter units for dx in the surface normal calculation formulas.

description.p: Indicates the intended distance in current filter units (i.e. as determined by the value of VectorFilter.PrimitiveUnits) for dx in the surface normal calculation formulas. This is equivalent to the first value of the SVG kernelUnitLength attribute.

If UnitX is not specified, the kernel unit is one unit of the client vector's coordinate system, regardless of VectorFilter.PrimitiveUnits. The appearance of the lighting then depends on the size of the bump map in those units: the same graphic will look flatter when it is drawn larger in its own coordinate system, but not when it is magnified by a parent transform.

By specifying UnitX in bounding box units, the kernel becomes relative to the filter's bounds, which are measured on the same terms as BlurFX. A bump map that is blurred and lit in bounding box units will then have the same appearance at any size and display resolution.
The value must be greater than zero. Rather than resampling the bump map to the kernel grid, the surface gradient is measured per pixel and scaled to the kernel unit.

field.name: UnitY
field.comment: The intended distance in current filter units for dy in the surface normal calculation formulas.

description.p: Indicates the intended distance in current filter units (i.e. as determined by the value of VectorFilter.PrimitiveUnits) for dy in the surface normal calculation formulas. This is equivalent to the second value of the SVG kernelUnitLength attribute. The value must be greater than zero. Refer to UnitX for further details.

field.name: Wrap
field.comment: Extends the diffuse light of the COMBINED type past the terminator.

description.p: Wrap lighting softens the transition from light to shade, as on wax, paper and skin, where light scattered within the material reaches areas that face slightly away from the light. The diffuse term N.L is replaced with (N.L + Wrap) / (1 + Wrap), so that faces turned up to asin(Wrap) past the terminator receive some light.

Unlike the other lighting extensions, a non-zero value changes the brightness of flat surfaces: a flat surface under a distant light at elevation E receives (sin E + Wrap) / (1 + Wrap) of the diffuse light instead of sin E.

Faces that turn away from a distant light lie in the surface's own shadow, which would cancel the wrapped light when the SHADOWS feature is enabled. For the diffuse light of those faces, shadows are instead cast by the light raised by the wrap angle, asin(Wrap), so that a face is not darkened by its own slope. Surfaces that face the light keep their shadows unchanged. As a surface cannot tell its own shadow from one cast by a distant feature, a face that turns away from the light is also lit inside a cast shadow, if the feature that casts it rises less than the wrap angle above the light. At a Wrap of 1, or wherever the raised light is within 1 degree of overhead, such faces receive no shadow. The extra shadow pass increases the cost of the effect.
The default is 0, and the value must be between 0 and 1. The diffuse and specular types ignore this field.

field.name: XMLDef
field.comment: Returns an SVG element that describes the effect.

description.p: The result is a complete element. The lighting types use feDiffuseLighting, feSpecularLighting or xvg:feLighting and include their light sources. The NORMAL type uses xvg:feNormalMap and includes the primitive subregion and surface settings. Settings that SVG cannot express are written as xvg: attributes when they differ from their defaults. These include xvg:features if Features is not ALL, and xvg:cavity, xvg:detail and xvg:penumbra for Cavity, Detail and Penumbra, xvg:normalConvention and xvg:normalStrength for NormalConvention and NormalStrength, xvg:occlusionChannel and xvg:occlusionStrength for OcclusionChannel and OcclusionStrength, xvg:roughnessChannel for RoughnessChannel, and xvg:ambient for Ambient. The COMBINED type also writes metalness, fresnel, wrap, anisotropy and anisotropyAngle for Metalness, Fresnel, Wrap, Anisotropy and AnisotropyAngle when they are not zero, and matcapMode="light" if MatcapMode is LIGHT. The standard elements carry these settings as xvg:combinedMetalness and similar. An SVG-loaded matcap keeps its original relative reference so the image can be reloaded from the same document folder. For API-loaded images MatcapPath must be document-relative. A matcap supplied as a Matcap bitmap returns ERR::NoSupport during serialisation. A MatcapEffect binding is written by VectorFilter.EffectXML as xvg:matcap="#name", or xvg:combinedMatcap on the standard elements, where name is the producer's result. The attributes of xvg:feLighting and xvg:feNormalMap are written without the prefix because the elements are in the Kōtuku namespace. The document must declare the prefix, for example xmlns:xvg="http://www.kotuku.dev/xmlns/svg".

Each light is written as a child element, in the order in which the lights were added. The options of SetLightOptions are written on the light's element as xvg:colour, xvg:intensity, xvg:range and xvg:shadows, when they differ from their defaults. The intensity of the first light is Intensity.
VectorFilter.EffectXML includes primary, albedo and named map bindings and assigns result names to referenced effects.

constants.comment: Enhanced lighting features for the LightingFX class. These apply only when the enhanced pipeline is in use; refer to LightingFX.Features.
constants.const: Synonym for DEQUANTISE | SHARPEN | CAVITY | DETAIL | SHADOWS | SPECULAR_AA | DEQUANTISE_WIDE | LOCAL_SHADOWS
Darken narrow creases and pits in proportion to their curvature.
Smooth areas that vary by no more than one alpha level, removing the terraces of 8-bit heights.
Reconstruct gently sloping terraces in 8-bit heights before DEQUANTISE smooths other samples.
Give fine detail more relief than broad shapes.
Point and spot lights cast shadows from raised areas of the surface.
Distant lights cast shadows from raised areas of the surface.
Measure slopes with a 4th-order gradient that keeps more of the detail in narrow features. If not set, the SVG Sobel kernel is used.
Widen specular highlights where the surface varies within a pixel, preventing sparkle at high exponents.

constants.comment: Options for a light of the LightingFX class; refer to LightOptions.
constants.const: The light uses its own Colour in place of the colour of the effect.
The light casts no shadows.
Distant light source.
Point light source.
Spot light source.

constants.comment: Lighting algorithm for the LightingFX class.
constants.const: Light an albedo with diffuse, specular and ambient light in a single pass, producing a finished surface.
Select diffuse lighting.
Write the surface normals to RGB for use as a displacement map.
Select specular lighting.

constants.comment: Channel selection for scalar maps, such as height, ambient occlusion and roughness maps.
constants.const: The alpha channel.
The blue channel.
The green channel, which is the roughness channel of a packed ORM map.
The luminance of the stored red, green and blue values, weighted 0.2126, 0.7152 and 0.0722.
The red channel. This is the default, and the occlusion channel of a packed ORM map.

constants.comment: Uses of the matcap of LightingFX's COMBINED type; refer to LightingFX.MatcapMode.
constants.const: Use the matcap as the diffuse light, in place of the diffuse light of the light sources.
Add the matcap to the specular light as a reflection of the environment. This is the default.

constants.comment: Axis conventions for normal maps read by LightingFX and DisplacementFX.
constants.const: DisplacementFX only. Read the map as a normal map only if it was written by LightingFX with type NORMAL, otherwise as colour.
Green encodes Y in image axes, increasing downwards. Used by DirectX and by LightingFX's NORMAL type.
Green encodes Y increasing upwards, as in OpenGL. The green component is negated when read.

struct.name: LightGeometry
struct.comment: Type, position and direction of one light of LightingFX, read by GetLight() and applied by SetLight().
struct.field: The kind of light. SetLight() requires the light's current type.
Distant lights: direction angle on the XY plane (clockwise), in degrees from the X axis.
Distant lights: direction angle from the XY plane towards the Z axis, in degrees.
Point and spot lights: X location of the light source.
Point and spot lights: Y location of the light source.
Point and spot lights: Z location of the light source.
Spot lights: X location of the light source's target.
Spot lights: Y location of the light source's target.
Spot lights: Z location of the light source's target.
Spot lights: exponent controlling the focus of the light.
Spot lights: limiting cone angle in degrees, or 0 for no cone.

struct.name: LightOptions
struct.comment: Options for one light of LightingFX, applied by SetLightOptions().
struct.field: Colour of the light if Flags includes COLOUR, in the colour space of LightingFX.Colour. Alpha is ignored.
Multiplies the colour of the light. Zero or greater; 1 leaves the light unchanged.
Distance at which a point or spot light reaches zero, in the units of its z coordinate, or 0 for an unlimited light.
